name: countdown
author: CVER Inc.
calls: GET <data-src> — only for a root that carries `data-src` (or, on a page whose `<html lang>` matches, `data-src-<language>`, which is then the URL used instead), and then the bundle's only network call: one fetch per such root, sent once on load, with no request body and no header other than `Accept: application/json`; the browser's default credential behaviour for that URL applies. A root with no feed for the page's language makes no network call at all. The response is read as an events feed (`{ calendar, events }`) and its text is written into the host's `data-event` elements as text; the only URLs it can put in a link are an http(s) location or URL from an event, a map search for an event's place, and an add-to-calendar link built from the event. A non-ok response, a network failure, no answer within eight seconds, a body that is not JSON, and a feed with no event still to come are all handled the same way — see `without`.
without: requires nothing. A root without `data-src` calls nothing: without the script it stays exactly as authored — an author who marked it `hidden` sees nothing, otherwise the host's own markup shows with empty unit elements — and a `data-deadline` without an explicit offset is treated the same way: nothing is mounted and nothing is changed. A root with `data-src` whose feed is unreachable or slow to answer, or holds no event still to come whose start and end the feed could place, counts to its `data-deadline` when it has a valid one and is otherwise left exactly as authored, its `data-event` and `data-event-href` elements keeping the host's own text and links. The words it writes for units, dates and time zones are the browser's own (Intl) in the page's language; where the browser has none the host's text stays.
